newsitem.title: USA: Great Lakes hoping for flights Thursday.
newsitem.headline: Great Lakes hoping for flights Thursday.

text.p: Great Lakes Aviation Ltd, a commuter airline that grounded flights after federal inspectors alleged it operated "unairworthy aircraft," said it hopes to have limited flights in the air by Thursday.
"Assuming everything goes as we expect it to, we hope to have some limited operations in the air on Thursday," Dick Fontaine, senior vice president of marketing for Great Lakes, said in an interview.

Great Lakes, whose operations are based in Spencer, Iowa, voluntarily suspended all flights Friday evening after the Federal Aviation Administration told the carrier it planned to suspend its operating authority, the regulatory agency said Saturday.

Great Lakes, which operates commuter flights for UAL Corp's United Airlines, as well as for Midway Airlines, said it was having aircraft inspections done at its Spencer facility and was concentrating on getting the newer planes among its 53 aircraft back in the air.
"If we could get three airplanes up in the air (Thursday), then we would have between 20 and 25 flights," Fontaine said.

An FAA spokeswoman said the regulatory agency has been working on a consent decree with Great Lakes, which operates as United Express and Midway Connection. The decree would outline the steps Great Lakes needs to take to resume operation, she said.
The FAA said Saturday that inspections found the airline allowed personnel who were not properly trained and qualified to perform aircraft maintenance.
Great Lakes said over the weekend it had been in discussions with the FAA about the safety of its aircraft, but did not expect the FAA to suspend its operating authority.

"This process accelerated in the last couple of days," Great Lakes chief executive Douglas Voss told Reuters Saturday. "We did not expect it. We had discussions and due to their (FAA) lack of confidence in status of the aircraft, we elected that we would take the airplanes into maintenance bases and essentially begin a review to be certain there's no question regarding the airworthiness of the aircraft."
Great Lakes shares were down 1/2 at 3/4 Monday.
